notes: No corpus contains a pMARS/CoreWars/Redcode task - the lexical 'corewars/warrior' hits were all Taskwarrior false positives, and the TMax shortlist for this packet is essentially noise (citation-graph/SQLite tasks). I judged on the two real transferable axes: (1) writing correct programs in a low-level/esoteric assembly or VM instruction set, and (2) designing a competitive game agent tuned to beat opponents. TerminalWorld's tw_346220 (write assembly in a simulator's ISA and run it) is the single closest task in the whole pool. RTS has a large, high-quality cluster of hand-written ARM64-assembly authoring tasks that transfer the low-level-programming skill directly. SWE-Rebench's axelrod-python (Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma tournament strategies) and pelita (competitive bot game) uniquely capture the beat-your-opponents axis, though as library bug fixes their task_form is weak. SWE-Smith is the weakest corpus here (parsers/binary-format codecs are the best proxies, all overall 1-2). final_top10 is intentionally dominated by the assembly/VM-authoring axis with one game-strategy representative at rank 10.
